title: Phytoplankton seasonal succession in response to environmental drivers in the eastern English Channel: a revised Margalef Mandala for a highly turbulent region
content:
Abstract
Classical conceptual models or Mandalas may explain phytoplankton dynamics in ecosystems where succession from diatoms to dinoflagellates is commonly observed. In highly turbulent, diatom-Phaeocystis dominated waters of the eastern English Channel, however, these models may not be fully applicable. This study identifies environmental states and key drivers of phytoplankton seasonal succession in the eastern English Channel by integrating high-frequency hydrological and physicochemical data with low-frequency phytoplankton observations. Multilevel Spectral Clustering (M-SC) was applied to a high-frequency dataset to identify environmental states, which were then linked to a phytoplankton abundance dataset. Eight environmental states were identified, including recurrent, rare, and extreme events, revealing a succession from winter conditions dominated by tychopelagic and other diatoms (e.g. Skeletonema costatum, Thalassiosira, Thalassionema), to spring blooms driven by Phaeocystis globosa and Pseudo-nitzschia. A transition period precedes summer assemblages dominated by diatoms (e.g. Rhizosolenia, Chaetoceros, Guinardia, Leptocylindrus). Diatoms persist year-round with spring blooms of P. globosa, highlighting their ecological plasticity, while dinoflagellates remain scarce. Inspired by Margalef Mandala, a Margalef-based visualization diagram was developed. The revised Mandala maps phytoplankton across six environmental variables including nitrate and nitrite, phosphate, silicate, photosynthetically active radiation, turbidity, and nitrate-to-phosphate ratio. This study may provide new insights to predict phytoplankton assemblages in the context of climate change and anthropogenic pressure.
